title: Arkret Account Subscribe Frame
description: Single NDJSON frame on the ak.self.account.stream.subscribe streaming channel (GET /_arkret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, presence, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ak.self.events.stream.subscribe (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ak:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

device_lists.description: Principal DID sets whose authoritative device list changed or left the caller's visibility scope on `delta` frames.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

notifications.description: Account-private notification projection deltas on `delta` frames. These are not Realm Events and are authorized by the authenticated account context rather than realm_id visibility.

agent_signer_evidence_bundle.description: Bounded signer-evidence sidecar for Agent-authored Events in this delta. Clients MUST verify each evidence item before caching or using it.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ak.self.events.query.scan for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ak.self.account.stream.subscribe` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

notification_kind.description: Closed notification type. Agent runtime approvals reuse the registered notification type `agent`.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ak:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ak.self.device_messages.query.list?after=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ak.self.device_messages.query.list?after=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

ordered_log_conflict_diagnostic.description: User-visible audit diagnostic for an ordered log issuer equivocation. The loser remains in canonical history but is excluded from timeline.events and the joined state leaf.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

preview_only.description: Fallback path of client-sync.md §5.2: when timeline.limited=true and the server does not return realm_sync_entry.state_at_window_start, it MUST set preview_only=true. Clients then render window-start events as preview only.

ordered_log_conflicts.description: Audit-visible ordered log equivocations affecting this timeline window. Clients MUST NOT render loser events as ordinary messages; they MAY expose these records in conflict/audit UI.

members.description: Lightweight roster hint derived from effective ak.member.state, effective ak.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

members_limited.description: True when members[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

members_next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the timeline window start. NOT part of state hash, frontier, or causal graph.

collaboration_role.description: Projection-only strong Realm role, emitted only after the server validates the registered Realm profile and discriminator.

subject_id.description: Optional disclosed principal / holder DID for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ak.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ak.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ak.find.directory.query.list_handles_for_subject.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
